Test your knowledge of the material on [discrete distributions](../lectures/02-Discrete.pdf) in the following quiz to see how much you learned.
This is **entirely private for you**---no records are kept of your performance. When you've answered all the question, click on the Submit Quiz button
to see how you've done, and perhaps get pointers to things you should review.

<div class="quiz-container">

<form id="quizForm">

<div class="question" id="q1">
<h3>1. What are the assumptions necessary for a variable to be distributed as a binomial distribution?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="a" id="q1a"> <label for="q1a">a) The variable must be binary</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="b" id="q1b"> <label for="q1b">b) The variable must be discrete</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="c" id="q1c"> <label for="q1c">c) The variable must have a fixed number of trials</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="d" id="q1d"> <label for="q1d">d) All of the above</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp1"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q2">
<h3>2. How does the skewness of a binomial variable relate to its parameters <em>n</em> and <em>p</em>?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="a" id="q2a"> <label for="q2a">a) Skewness = n p</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="b" id="q2b"> <label for="q2b">b) Skewness = n/p</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="c" id="q2c"> <label for="q2c">c) Skewness = p (1-p) / n</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="d" id="q2d"> <label for="q2d">d) Skewness = p^2 / n</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp2"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q3">
<h3>3. When would you use a negative binomial distribution over a Poisson distribution?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="a" id="q3a"> <label for="q3a">a) When the number of trials is fixed</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="b" id="q3b"> <label for="q3b">b) When the variance exceeds the mean</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="c" id="q3c"> <label for="q3c">c) When there are negative counts in the data</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="d" id="q3d"> <label for="q3d">d) When the parameter p differs substantially from 0.5</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp3"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q4">
<h3>4. How does the mean and variance of a Poisson distribution relate to its parameter λ?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q4" value="a" id="q4a"> <label for="q4a">a) Mean = λ, Variance = λ</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q4" value="b" id="q4b"> <label for="q4b">b) Mean = 1/λ, Variance = 1/λ^2</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q4" value="c" id="q4c"> <label for="q4c">c) Mean = 1/λ, Variance = λ</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q4" value="d" id="q4d"> <label for="q4d">d) Mean = λ, Variance = λ^2</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp4"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q5">
<h3>5. Which example is most likely to follow a log-series distribution?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q5" value="a" id="q5a"> <label for="q5a">a) Number of accidents at a busy intersection</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q5" value="b" id="q5b"> <label for="q5b">b) Counts of occurrences of distinct words in the books written by Jane Austen</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q5" value="c" id="q5c"> <label for="q5c">c) Number of births of males in Canadian families composed of 6 children</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q5" value="d" id="q5d"> <label for="q5d">d) Number of tosses of a coin required to get the first head</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp5"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q6">
<h3>6. Which of the following characterize the negative binomial distribution and the geometric distribution?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q6" value="a" id="q6a"> <label for="q6a">a) The negative binomial distribution models the number of failures before a specified number of successes</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q6" value="b" id="q6b"> <label for="q6b">b) The geometric distribution models the number of failures before the first success</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q6" value="c" id="q6c"> <label for="q6c">c) Both A and B</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q6" value="d" id="q6d"> <label for="q6d">d) Neither A nor B</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp6"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q7">
<h3>7. In what type of data might you use a negative binomial distribution?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q7" value="a" id="q7a"> <label for="q7a">a) Count data</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q7" value="b" id="q7b"> <label for="q7b">b) Binary data</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q7" value="c" id="q7c"> <label for="q7c">c) Continuous data</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q7" value="d" id="q7d"> <label for="q7d">d) Both A and B</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp7"></div>
</div>

<div class="question" id="q8">
<h3>8. What is the mean and variance of a variable distributed as a geometric distribution?</h3>
<div class="options">
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q8" value="a" id="q8a"> <label for="q8a">a) Mean = λ, Variance = λ</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q8" value="b" id="q8b"> <label for="q8b">b) Mean = 1/λ, Variance = 1/λ^2</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q8" value="c" id="q8c"> <label for="q8c">c) Mean = 1/λ, Variance = λ</label></div>
<div class="option"><input type="radio" name="q8" value="d" id="q8d"> <label for="q8d">d) Mean = λ, Variance = 1/λ^2</label></div>
</div>
<div class="explanation" id="exp8"></div>
</div>
